title: Reaching Peak of Singapore's Carbon Dioxide-equivalent Emissions
what_it_is: Reaching Peak of Singapore's Carbon Dioxide-equivalent Emissions

sections.label: Singapore's Second Update NDC
sections.summary: Singapore submitted its Second Update to its 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution, intending to reduce emissions to around 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2030 after peaking earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Singapore Government has just submitted Singapore's Second Update to our 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution, or NDC, to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In the submission, we indicated that Singapore intends to reduce emissions to around 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO2e) in 2030 after peaking our emissions earlier.

sections.label: Emissions peak year estimate
sections.summary: The Government estimates emissions will peak between 2025 and 2028, and remains committed to around 60 million tonnes in 2030 under the Green Plan's five pillars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As such, it is premature to announce a precise year in which our emissions will peak.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Government's best estimate is for our emissions to peak between 2025 and 2028, which will be earlier than our previous 2030 target, at around 65 million tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these uncertainties, we remain committed to achieving what we set out in the Second Update to our 2030 NDC – for our emissions in 2030 to be around 60 million tonnes, or five million tonnes lower than what we set out in the First Update in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: It is more than the total emissions from households today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have put in place a comprehensive package of mitigation measures under the five pillars of the Green Plan to achieve this.
